name: Turbopuffer
model: Namespaces of documents with vectors and attributes; vector, full-text (BM25) and hybrid search with filters over an HTTP API
engine_note: SPFresh centroid-based ANN index (few round trips suits object storage); WAL and index files on object storage (S3/GCS), cached on NVMe SSD and memory
consistency: A write returns only after it is durably in object storage (WAL). Queries are strongly consistent by default (see your own writes); an eventual option is faster but can be up to about an hour stale. Writes are batched about once per second per namespace.
scaling: Serverless, multi-tenant: storage in object storage, stateless query nodes cache hot namespaces; scales by many namespaces (one per tenant) and up to 256 shards per namespace.
version_note: Managed service with no public version numbers. Date is the last update of the vendor's architecture post (first published 2024-07-08). Site banner (2026-10) says 'turbopuffer v3 is coming', undated.
reach: Reach for it with many tenants or huge, mostly cold vector sets where storage cost dominates and a slow first query per namespace is acceptable.
avoid: Avoid when every query must be fast even on cold data, writes must be visible within milliseconds, or data must stay on your own servers without an enterprise deal.
escape: It stores very large or many-tenant vector sets on cheap object storage instead of Postgres disks and RAM.
chat: One namespace per user holding their message embeddings; idle users cost only object storage.
notes: CLAIM CHECK (c) 'Turbopuffer keeps vectors on object storage behind an SSD cache, trading a few milliseconds of latency for roughly an order of magnitude less cost per stored vector': PARTLY CORRECTED. Architecture verified: docs/architecture: 'After the first query, the namespace's documents are cached on NVMe SSD.' Latency trade is not 'a few milliseconds': a cold query is far slower. Docs: 'The first query to a namespace reads object storage directly and is slow (p50=874 ms for 1M documents), but subsequent, cached queries to that node are faster (p50=14 ms for 1M documents).' Cost: vendor claim only. Founder post (https://turbopuffer.com/blog/turbopuffer, 2024-07-08, updated 2026-03-05): 'in-memory storage at $2+ per GB ... triply replicated SSDs at 50% storage utilization which will run you $0.6 per GB ... object storage (like S3 or GCS) at around $0.02 per GB, with SSD caching at $0.1 per GB for frequently accessed data. That's up to 100x cheaper than memory for cold storage, and 6-20x cheaper for warm storage!' Homepage: 'fast, 10x cheaper, and extremely scalable'. So 'about an order of magnitude cheaper' matches the vendor's own figures (6-20x warm, up to 100x cold, vs RAM-based stores); suggested wording: 'warm queries cost a few ms (p50 14 ms), a cold first query close to a second (p50 874 ms); vendor claims 6-20x cheaper warm, up to 100x cold, than RAM-based stores'. Durability quote: 'If a write returns successfully, data is guaranteed to be durably written to object storage.' Write latency 'p50= 165 ms for 500kB'; 'Each namespace can currently write 1 WAL entry per second.' Consistency: 'strong consistency by default'; eventual mode 'staleness of up to about one hour can be observed in the worst case' (quoted via fetch summary). Index: 'Vector indexes are based on SPFresh', 'a centroid-based approximate nearest neighbour index'. Limits page: max 256 shards per namespace, max dense dimensions 10,752. Pricing page lists plan minimums ($16, $256 per month) and BYOC/single-tenancy on enterprise; no per-GB prices extracted. No Jepsen analysis.
